label: D2 after a rewarded repeat of a2, early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (DELAY_2), only when this trial chose a2 (in_action == 2), the previous trial was rewarded (r1 seen at this D1), and the agent stayed on a2 (previous choice a2 or window start). It is strongly tied to episode time: it fires in trials ~2-45 and essentially never after trial 50, so it acts like a slow drifting hidden-state term gating a reward-repeat signal. All variables are observed at D2 (the D2 action is the just-taken choice). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1 choices, after unrewarded trials, or after switches. Magnitude: per-activation mass is about 1.5x higher when the reached state is S1 (a rare transition after a2) than when it is S2, and top activations are rare-S1 trials following reward; activations also sit in the high-value bin. Remaining false positives are mostly early/late-boundary trials and some rewarded a2 stays where the unit stays below threshold.

issues: The predicate is missing a condition, and the gap is systematic rather than scattered noise. It ignores whether the previous trial's transition was common. Adding (prev_common == 0) to the original predicate selects 4712 dev steps with precision 0.022 (recall 0.003). That is about 4600 of the roughly 12.6k dev false positives. Requiring prev_common == 1 instead gives precision 0.847. So the unit fires after a rewarded *common* a2 trial (a2 -> S2, rewarded), not after any rewarded a2 trial. A rewarded rare a2 -> S1 trial followed by repeating a2 does not drive it.

So the label 'rewarded repeat of a2' overclaims. The real condition is narrower: the previous trial was a2 -> S2 (common) and rewarded, or the trial is the window's first, and the agent chose a2 again.
The original predicate's low precision at rel +1 (0.48) came from the same cause. With prev_common != 0 added, rel +1 precision rises to 0.82, in line with the other positions (0.80-0.88).

Claims that check out: the unit is active only at D2 (zero activations at D1 and GO); it never fires after unrewarded trials (prev_reward 0: 0 activations), never after a1 choices (0), and almost never after switches (23 activations). The episode-time claim holds: 0.08-0.10 active rate in trials 0-39, 0.026 in trials 40-49, 99 activations in 50-59 and none after. The magnitude claim also holds: per activation, S1 (rare) steps carry about 1.46x the mass of S2 steps.

Residual weaker structure: when good == S1 (hidden), precision under the refined predicate drops to 0.65, but that slice is small (2549 predicted). The unit fires more often in start_high == 0 episodes (S2 good first), which is consistent with S2 being good early in the episode.
